summary: The source inventory for Madre de Dios contains no law, ordinance, enforcement record, institution or incident specific to the department, so no region-specific signal was identified and the national assessment applies to a trans visitor there.
tangentialFactors:
All three sources held for this department are national in scope, and each states expressly that it records no Madre de Dios-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding. Their subject matter — the congressional restriction on public restroom access approved in committee in February 2025 and by the Plenary on 2 April 2025, and the national tally of 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases recorded over 2020–2023 — is national-level material carried by the Peru record rather than by this department.

No comparative or adjacent-jurisdiction material for Madre de Dios was sourced: the inventory holds nothing on neighbouring departments, on cross-border movement through the department, or on how its enforcement practice differs from other Peruvian regions.
localsOnly: No resident-facing fact specific to Madre de Dios was identified in the inventory: nothing on departmental or provincial government practice, local police conduct, regional health or education facilities, or documented treatment of trans residents of the department is sourced here.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved and not sourced: whether the national public-restroom restriction has been applied, enforced or challenged within Madre de Dios; whether any trans-specific incident, arrest, complaint or protection measure has occurred in the department; and whether regional authorities there have issued guidance, training or facility rules bearing on trans people. The inventory provides no evidence either way, and the absence of a documented department-level case should not be read as evidence that none has occurred.
